_comment: Settlement and site types placed during world generation. glyph/colour are how they show on the overworld map.

cellars: Cut stone, and a smell of old grain and older water. Somebody built this to keep things in.
Storerooms and passages under a building that is no longer there. The walls still hold the marks of shelves.
Low vaults, a floor of packed earth over flagstones, and a draught from somewhere you cannot see.
Barrel hoops rusting in a heap, a well-head capped with a stone, and rats that do not run from the light.
A brick undercroft, its arches black with soot, and at the far end a door somebody nailed shut from this side.
Sacks rotted to the shape of what was in them, and a trapdoor that someone has oiled lately.
The vaults go further than any house above could need. Whoever dug them was hiding more than wine.
Empty wine racks, a smell of vinegar and mould, and footprints in the dust that go one way only.
crypt: Shelves of stone with names worn off them, and the particular cold of a place built for the dead.
A passage of stacked coffins, and dust that has not been walked through in a hundred years.
Burial niches, three deep, and the smell of dry bone and lime.
Effigies on the lids, their faces chiselled away by someone who did not want them remembered.
A painted ceiling, flaking: saints, or kings, with the eyes scratched out.
Iron gates rusted open, and beyond them the long dark rows of the family who paid for all this.
Candle stubs on every ledge, some of them not very old. Somebody still comes down here.
The air is dry as paper. Grave goods lie where they were left, and nobody has dared to take them.
tower: Boards over stone, a stairway going the wrong way, and the mark on the floor where a circle was drawn.
Rooms stacked above and below one another, all of them empty, all of them recently swept.
Old timbers, chalk marks on the walls, and shelves where books used to be.
A spiral of worn steps, a smell of lamp oil and ink, and windows bricked up from the inside.
Glass jars on a shelf, most of them broken, the rest holding things it is better not to look at closely.
Star charts nailed to the walls, gone brown with damp, and a brass instrument nobody could name.
A study with its door torn off. Burnt pages drift in the corners like dead leaves.
Every doorway is carved with the same sign, and every one of the signs has been defaced.
hideout: Bedrolls, a fire pit, and picked bones. People live here, and they are not far.
A dug-out hall with sacking for doors and a smell of wet wool and smoke.
Rough-cut passages, propped with stolen beams, and boots by the entrance.
Crates with the marks of three different merchants, a dice board, and a pot still warm on the coals.
A smugglers' cut under the hill, and a lookout's stool by a crack that shows the road.
Stolen hangings nailed up against the damp, and a heap of empty purses in a corner.
Somebody has scratched a tally on the wall. There are a great many marks.
Snares, spare boots, a barrel of something sour, and an empty gibbet cage hanging from a beam.
temple: The air is thick, and the carvings are of nothing you can put a name to.
Somebody has been at pains to hide this: a hall under the earth, swept clean, and wax on every ledge.
Stone worn smooth by knees, and a smell of incense over something worse.
An altar black with old offerings, and a statue whose face has been covered with a sack.
Pews cut from the living rock, facing a wall of carvings that seem to move at the edge of the light.
A hymn is painted on the walls in a script you do not know, round and round, never ending.
Bowls of ash, chains on the pillars, and a drain in the floor before the altar.
The silence down here has weight. Even your breath sounds like an intrusion.
cave: Water somewhere, dripping, and the cold coming up out of the rock.
Passages gnawed out by water over a long time, going down into the dark.
Wet stone, bats, and a floor that slopes the wrong way.
A cave mouth widening into a hall of pale stone that drips like candle wax.
The bones of small things are scattered by the entrance, gnawed clean and white.
A cold stream runs across the floor and vanishes under a lip of rock. The air tastes of iron.
Roots hang through the roof, and something has worn a path along the wall that is not a man's.
The roof comes down to a crawl, then opens into a dark too large for your light to find its edges.
warren: Low tunnels, dug small and dug badly, and a stink of crowding.
A warren of passages, floors trodden to mud, with bones and rubbish kicked into the corners.
Tunnels propped with anything to hand, and the sound of something moving two turns away.
Totems of bone and feathers at every fork, and the walls smeared with signs in something brown.
Sleeping holes scraped into the walls, dozens of them, and the reek of unwashed bodies and rot.
A cooking pit with a pot the size of a cartwheel, and bones in it you would rather not name.
Stolen things everywhere, hoarded without sense: a church bell, a ploughshare, a child's doll.
The tunnels twist back on themselves, low and narrow, dug by things that fight in the dark.
lair: The rock is scorched, the air is dry and hot, and everything here is too big.
A hall not built but melted, and a smell of metal and burning.
The floor is scattered with the armour of people who came before you, most of it opened like a nutshell.
Claw marks gouged a hand deep into the stone, and a smell of something huge and alive.
The bones of cattle, of horses, of men, heaped against the walls like driftwood after a flood.
Coins crunch underfoot here and there, spilled and forgotten, as if gold were nothing much.
Heat breathes out of the deep in slow waves, like the breath of a sleeper.
Nothing small lives here. Nothing has dared to, for a long time.

any: Water drips somewhere behind you, and keeps time with nothing.
A draught comes from somewhere that should not have a somewhere.
Grit shifts overhead, and a little of it comes down.
Your light finds a mark on the wall: somebody counted days here.
Something skitters out of the light and does not come back.
The passage breathes: in for a while, then out.
A bone, old and gnawed, is underfoot before you see it.
Far off, or not far off, stone moves against stone.
cellars: A barrel hoop lies rusted into the floor, the staves long gone.
Your foot goes through something soft that used to be a sack of grain.
A rat has made a nest out of somebody's ledger.
crypt: A name on a shelf is still legible, and it is a common name still used above.
Dust lifts where nothing has walked, and settles again.
One of the stone lids is off, and set carefully aside, which is worse than broken.
tower: A stair goes up into rubble, and stops.
Chalk lines on the floor, half scuffed away, and none of them are straight.
Glass grits under your boots, coloured glass, from a window that is not here.
hideout: A fire pit, still warm enough to notice.
Somebody has scratched a tally into the door frame and then given up.
Bedding, recently slept in, and pulled back in a hurry.
temple: The carvings here follow you round the room, which is a trick of the light.
A bowl of something dark, set in a niche, and not old.
The air tastes of old incense and something under it.
cave: Water has been at this rock for longer than anything above has been standing.
The floor slopes away and the sound of falling water comes up out of it.
A pool, still as glass, and nothing living in it.
warren: The ceiling comes down and you go on bent double for a while.
Something has been dragged along this floor, repeatedly, in one direction.
The stink gets worse, and then better, which tells you where they sleep.
lair: The rock here is glazed with old heat.
A scale the size of your palm, half trodden into the floor.
Bones, big ones, cracked open for the marrow.

ruin.name: ruin
ruin.desc: Tumbled walls and empty windows: something stood here once.

cave.name: cave
cave.desc: A cave mouth, black and cold-breathed.

barrow.name: barrow
barrow.desc: A long grassy mound with a stone-lined entrance: an old grave of kings or chieftains.

tower.name: old tower
tower.desc: A lonely tower, roofless, its stair open to the sky.
